newsitem.title: USA: SBC gets Oklahoma's backing for long-distance service.
newsitem.headline: SBC gets Oklahoma's backing for long-distance service.

text.p: SBC Communications Inc.'s bid to be the first Baby Bell to break into the $80 billion long-distance market was boosted Friday when Oklahoma regulators backed its request to provide the service there.

The three-member Oklahoma Corporation Commission voted 2-1 to recommend that SBC be allowed to offer Oklahoma customers long-distance services, and forwarded its decision to the Federal Communications Commission, which has the final say.

SBC Chief Executive Officer Edward Whitacre welcomed the Oklahoma regulators' decision and said SBC would submit within 60 days an application to provide long-distance service in another of the states where it operates.
He did not say in which state the next application would be made. SBC, the parent of Southwestern Bell, operates in seven states, including California and Texas.

SBC's efforts to enter Oklahoma's long-distance market has been opposed by AT&T Corp., Sprint Corp., MCI Communications, Brooks Fiber Properties Inc. and Oklahoma's attorney general, among others, who argued that SBC had not yet opened its local telephone monopoly to competitors.

Under the 1996 communications law, SBC and other regional Bells must meet a 14-point checklist showing they have opened up their local monopolies before gaining FCC approval for long-distance services.
SBC's opponents are expected to continue their battle before the FCC, but Whitacre said he would respond.

"There are 90 companies approved to provide local service in our service area and they are doing it. If they say they are not, I can prove they are," he told Reuters after the company's annual meeting in San Antonio.

SBC had suffered a setback when an Oklahoma administrative law judge last week recommended its long-service request be rejected because it had not met a federal checklist for entry. But the Oklahoma Corporation Commission ruled in favour of SBC during a public meeting on Friday morning.
